newsitem.title: SPAIN: Slain Spanish politician laid to rest.
newsitem.headline: Slain Spanish politician laid to rest.

text.p: Miguel Angel Blanco, a young politician kidnapped and killed by Basque separatist guerrillas, was buried in his hometown on Monday in a solemn ceremony broadcast live on national television.
Blanco was entombed in a crypt at Ermua's cemetery before thousands of mourners, including Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Crown Prince Felipe, gathering to pay their last respects.
The casket was carried several km (miles) to the cemetery with hundreds of people filing behind.
Crowds, held back by red-jacketed Basque police, clapped and chanted "Miguel, Miguel, Miguel" and "Murderers! Murderers!" as his casket was carried through narrow streets.
Blanco's killing sparked an angry public outcry against the rebel group ETA, which has waged a violent 29-year struggle for an Basque independent homeland.
Blanco, 29, a low-ranking member of Spain's ruling party, was kidnapped last Thursday by ETA, which threatened to execute him in 48 hours if the government did not meet their demands.
He was found on Saturday dumped outside the Basque city of San Sebastian, his hands tied behind his back and two bullets lodged in his brain. He slipped into a coma and died before dawn on Sunday.
Over the weekend, historic numbers of Spaniards took to the streets to protest the kidnap and brutal killing.
As his funeral began on Monday, Spain came to a virtual standstill, with millions of people stopping work at noon to observe 10 minutes of silence.

Throughout the Basque region, thousands of people returned to the streets, some chanting "Basques yes, ETA no", and others clasping their hands behind their necks in a reference to ETA's method of shooting its victims in the nape of the neck.
